title: Reconstruction-v2 extrinsic MT evaluation — Table 3 structure
not_a_reproduction: New measurements generated by the reconstructed pipeline. These are not the published Table 3 values, are not a reproduction of them, and must not be tabulated alongside them.

experimental_design.matrix: 3 tokenizers x 3 seeds, one multilingual model per run
experimental_design.architecture: MarianMT 6+6 layers, 8 heads, d_model 512, FFN 2048, shared embeddings
experimental_design.vocab_note: Paper reports 63,050. The released MoVoC tokenizer contains 63,051 entries and was not modified; BPE and WordPiece were trained to 63,051 so vocabulary size is not a confound.

opus.note: OPUS/Tatoeba held-out sets as shipped in data/evaluation/
opus.type: supervised for am/ti; zero-shot for tig/gez

evaluation_datasets.separation_note: FLORES-200 and OPUS are reported separately and never merged.

metrics.aggregation: mean and sample standard deviation (ddof=1) over run-level scores across seeds; never over sentence-level scores

scientific_validity_caveat.training_converged: Final training loss 3.00-3.59 across the nine runs, against ~3.13 reported for a comparable from-scratch MarianMT trained with 5.5x more optimizer steps (416,040 vs 75,000).
scientific_validity_caveat.output_quality: All 18 FLORES cells: 1012/1012 unique hypotheses, 0% empty, no <unk> collapse, hypothesis/reference line counts aligned. However an automated detector flags repetition in several cells (see output_quality_flagged_seeds). Inspection shows two distinct causes: for MoVoC-Tok en-am the trigger is Ge'ez punctuation frequency (the sentence-final marker at 67% of tokens), which is a property of the language rather than collapse; for MoVoC-Tok en-ti and some BPE en-ti output there is genuine intra-sentence repetition.
scientific_validity_caveat.interpretation: BLEU is below 2 in every cell. These runs do not reach a translation regime comparable to a fully trained system, so the values support no ranking claim about the tokenizers in either direction.
